stories.title: Sabalenka interrupts US Open match against Rakhimova over cannabis smell
stories.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka’s straight-sets US Open win against Kamilla Rakhimova stopped by smell of cannabis. World number one Aryna Sabalenka had an unusual interruption during her US Open third-round match, stopping play to alert the umpire to a strong smell of cannabis drifting onto the Louis Armstrong Stadium court. Sabalenka, who had made a fast start to go 3-0 ahead before securing a straight-sets win against Uzbekistan’s Kamilla Rakhimova, raised the issue during her second service game on Friday, pointing out the smell before play resumed. “Someone is smoking weed,” top seed Sabalenka told umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore as she was serving 30-0 up. “Would you mind to… because it’s so strong.” Sabalenka later told reporters she was not objecting to anyone enjoying themselves, but asked for the smoking to be kept away from the court. “I was like, Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts,” a smiling Sabalenka said. “It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.” The odour of cannabis has become a familiar — if unwelcome — feature at Flushing Meadows, with players complaining about the distraction in the past. While smoking is not permitted inside the grounds, recreational cannabis is legal for adults 21 and older in New York, and smoke from people in the surrounding Flushing Meadows-Corona Park can drift into the tennis complex and onto the courts. Sabalenka said she had smelled cannabis before during the tournament but never so strongly during a match, with Friday’s wind apparently carrying the odour into the stadium. “That strong, yeah.

stories.title: Argentine auto industry struggles while Chinese EVs gain ground
stories.summary: Recent data from Argentina’s automotive industry paint a mixed picture. While the sector as a whole has not managed to return to last year’s levels, electric vehicles from Chinese manufacturers continue to gain market share. According to data from the Association of Automotive Manufacturers (in Spanish, AFAC), 39,381 vehicles were produced in August. Although this figure is a 26% increase compared to July, it’s also an 11% decline compared to August 2025. Total production for 2026 stood at 275,228 units (down 17.1% compared to 2025). “The August results show a recovery compared to July, although the year-over-year trend and year-to-date figures indicate that the sector continues to face a challenging environment,” ADEFA head Rodrigo Pérez Graziano said. Wholesale sales to dealerships followed the same trend. In August, 39,068 vehicles were sold (a 14.3% monthly increase, but a 24.5% drop compared to August 2025). For the year, 301,377 units were sold (24.8% less compared to the same period last year). Exports showed a more consistent scene, totaling 24,589 units (a 5.2% monthly increase and a slight 3.6% year-over-year decline). For 2026, they totaled 174,859 vehicles (0.9% raise). Pérez Graziano noted that, while export numbers confirm the automotive industry’s capacity, advancing “competitiveness” will be crucial in order to expand markets and create “better conditions for production, investment, and employment.”
